clue.text: Pancake landing's first thing tackled by the majority of WWII fliers

indicators.note: a letter tackled by a group is grabbed and held among them, so it goes inside
most of the word is kept and only its opening portion is dropped

parts.note: the Luftwaffe was the German air force in the Second World War

indicators.note: the first thing in the word landing is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wartime plane making a belly landing is set upon by enemy aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' drops LUFT from LUFTWAFFE, leaving WAFFE; 'tackled by' puts L, the first letter of 'landing', inside it. A pancake landing is a flat belly landing, a red herring for the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A waffle is a batter cake cooked in a gridded iron, a close cousin of the pancake.

clue.text: Loathe one in HMS Pinafore Covent Garden's mounted

parts.note: an AB, an able seaman, is a sailor serving on a ship such as HMS Pinafore

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means climbing upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: the Royal Opera House, ROH, stands in Covent Garden

explanation.surface: Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore is staged at Covent Garden, and somebody hates it.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; the Royal Opera House in London's Covent Garden is abbreviated ROH, and 'mounted' turns it up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to hate it intensely, a straight synonym of loathe.

clue.text: VVV?

wordplay.reading: V flanked by V and V

parts.note: Roman numeral V is 5; the central V has another V at each of its flanks

explanation.surface: Three Roman fives in a row, puzzling on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral for five, and each outer V sits at one side of the central one.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-a-side is a small-team form of football with five players per team.

clue.text: English/Latin translation's clause affecting Will

indicators.note: translating a word turns it into something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer translates an English and Latin clause that touches a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation's' signals the anagram. 'Will' is capitalised to pass as a name, but it is a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: An entail is a legal settlement restricting who may inherit property, written into a will or deed.

clue.text: Tofu head smoked, lacking energy

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: smoked meat or fish is cured
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A smoked tofu dish lacks punch, by a diner's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' removes E from CURED to leave CURD.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd is the other name for tofu, pressed curds of soya milk.

clue.text: Sourcing bad muck to be broadcast in a lift?

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid sourcing dirt has it aired on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals rearranging all fifteen letters of SOURCING BAD MUCK; 'to be' is link. The definition is by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Muzak played quietly in elevators is the classic case of unobtrusive ambient music.

clue.text: He's likely to forget taking part in 'Courcais en Marche!' uprising

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
taking part in means the answer is a part of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful takes part in a march, a French-sounding uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'taking part' in the definition; it is the indicator, 'taking part in', for letters inside the quoted words. 'uprising' then reads CAISENMA up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss, so prone to forgetting.

clue.text: Taxi driver's bottom pierced by tip of elephant trunk

indicators.note: a thing pierced by another has it pushed inside it

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cabbie's backside is jabbed by an elephant's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: CAB plus R, the bottom of 'driver', with E, the 'tip of elephant', 'pierced' in. The definition is the last word, not the elephant's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games.

clue.text: Blunder in Times after file item got in a jam

indicators.note: after puts the jam-making half behind the file in this down clue

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

indicators.note: the blunder goes inside the word for times

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, three by four
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A newspaper blunder after a filed item lands the writer in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is multiplication (three by four). 'in a jam' is literal: the fruit goes into the preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspberries are a fruit commonly boiled down into preserves, so one is a component of that spread.

clue.text: Criminally cheat in shielding tax area guarded by Swiss

indicators.note: shielding means wrapping around, so the scrambled letters surround the tax
acting criminally means acting crookedly, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A tax dodger shelters money in an area guarded by Swiss banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminally' rearranges CHEAT IN into THE + ICAN, split around the tax. The Swiss suggest bank vaults, but they are the Pope's guards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss Guard is the papal army protecting the Vatican City state.

clue.text: Item on Fox trashing Republican president

indicators.note: trashing says a letter is thrown away from the word

parts.note: the brush is the tail of a fox

explanation.surface: A Fox News item lays into a Republican president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashing' removes R from BRUSH. Fox looks like the news network.
explanation.definitionFit: Two US presidents bore the name George Bush, father and son.

clue.text: Daughter studying with some apprehension

parts.note: reading a subject means studying it at university

explanation.surface: A daughter approaches her studies nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading a subject is the British way of saying one studies it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading means fearing something to come, regarding it with anxious anticipation.

clue.text: Astrolabes unfortunately in pieces, leaving flashing light

indicators.note: broken in pieces, the letters of the instrument are reassembled differently

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Antique astrolabes lie broken, losing their gleam.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: ASTROLABES 'in pieces', 'leaving' ALAS, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp that gives rapid repeated flashes.

clue.text: Tehrani regularly flying one further east?

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: A man from Tehran flies eastwards on a regular service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'Tehrani'. Thailand lies east of Iran, hence 'further east'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a native of Thailand, which lies well to the east of Iran.

clue.text: 9 occasionally emits this exclamation

definitions.meaning: the Vatican sends up white smoke when a new pope is elected

explanation.surface: The papal state sometimes lets out a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath of astonishment, and literally the smoke from a papal conclave.

clue.text: Old park-keeper, Head of Yeovil Conservatory

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A retired park-keeper and a Yeovil headteacher meet in a conservatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeovil is a town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-walled garden building, originally for growing citrus trees, a form of conservatory.

clue.text: Set ventriloquist's hat decoration on chest

indicators.note: a ventriloquist cannot move the lips for B, so says it as G, the famous gottle of geer

parts.note: a bobble is a woolly ball on top of a hat
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's dummy has a bobble hat placed on top of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ventriloquists notoriously render B as G, so BOBBLE comes out GOGGLE, placed 'on' (above) BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Gogglebox is British slang for a television, a TV set.

clue.text: Boarding budget-fare Filipinos capsized small boat

indicators.note: in a down clue a capsized run of letters is turned upside down, read bottom to top
boarding means getting inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: Filipinos on a cheap ferry capsize and take to a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' takes TFAREFIL from 'budget-fare Filipinos'; 'capsized' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A liferaft is a small inflatable craft for escaping a sinking vessel.

clue.text: Sugar-coated Ginger Spice from the Maghreb?

indicators.note: a coating goes round the outside, so one name wraps the other

parts.note: Alan Sugar is a British businessman of TV's The Apprentice
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A sugar-coated ginger spice from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' and 'Ginger Spice' look like confectionery and seasoning; they are Alan Sugar and Geri Halliwell. Maghreb is northwest Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is one of the Maghreb countries of northwest Africa, so an Algerian comes from there.

clue.text: State with Portuguese flavour home to Yankee artist

indicators.note: a place home to something holds it inside

parts.note: Goa is an Indian state that was a Portuguese colony
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American painter makes his home in a state with Portuguese influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Goa was a Portuguese colony until 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: Soprano, good for learner, upset old king

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, read bottom to top
for means one letter standing in place of another

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano
L is for learner, as on British learner plates

explanation.surface: A soprano, good in place of a learner, upsets an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: G replaces L in TREBLE giving TREBGE, and 'upset' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Egbert was a ninth-century King of Wessex, often called the first English king.

clue.text: Idiot reportedly looks at jury in Edinburgh

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: reportedly means the next word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A fool, it's said, eyes the jury in Scotland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ASS followed by the sound of EYES says the answer. In Scots law the assize was the jury itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish legal usage an assize meant the body of jurors trying a case.

clue.text: Turning puce, I freeze over

indicators.note: turning means these letters change into another order

explanation.surface: Going purple with cold, someone freezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges PUCE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become covered by a frozen layer.

clue.text: Chap taking on legal manoeuvring, straight-talking fellow?

indicators.note: taking on means holding within, so the scrambled word goes inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: manoeuvring things moves them around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man takes on legal manoeuvring, being a plain speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges LEGAL into AGELL, which MAN is 'taking on'. 'Straight-talking' is a pun on strait.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan gave his name to the Strait of Magellan, so he is a fellow known for a strait.

clue.text: Leaders of African city conducted round another African city

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Visitors are shown round one African city, then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' takes the initials of five words; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Solid Tory base

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: The Conservatives' solid core of voters.
explanation.walkthrough: The mathematical constant e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a geometric solid with a circular base tapering to a point.

clue.text: Get lippy with wife on vacation in miserable snack bar

indicators.note: in says one part sits inside the other
a miserable state is a wretched mess, so the letters are jumbled
a vacated word is emptied of its middle, keeping only the ends

explanation.surface: A woman away on holiday is cheeky to staff in a dreary snack bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'wife' to WE, placed 'in' the rearranged SNACK BAR, ANSRBACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer back is to retort cheekily, which is being insolent or mouthy.

clue.text: Tyrannical Democrat in charge smuggling ecstasy tablets and marijuana

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so tablets of it are Es
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A senior Democrat is caught smuggling drugs, behaving like a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for an ecstasy tablet, so 'tablets' makes it plural; the drugs sit between the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler, so despotic behaviour is tyrannical.

clue.text: HMRC chap Spooner's browned off, completely?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: to the max means completely
to tan is to brown in the sun

explanation.surface: A tax inspector is thoroughly fed up, according to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening letters of MAX and TAN. HMRC is Britain's tax authority, HM Revenue and Customs. 'Browned off' looks like fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxman is an official collecting taxes, as employed by the UK revenue service.
